id_and_class.summary: Jeffrey Mishlove holds that consciousness is fundamental and that the brain filters, localizes, and constrains a wider universal mind instead of producing experience. He rests the view on idealism, chosen for parsimony, and on the convergence of nine lines of anomalous evidence, from psi experiments and near-death experiences to reincarnation cases and mediumship, which he takes to make survival of bodily death expected rather than anomalous.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Universal Mind Filtered by the Brain

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the basic nature of a mindlike universe. Personal awareness is a localized portion of a wider mentality-at-large, admitted through the brain.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Following William James’s transmission theory, the brain works as a filter or reducing valve that admits into awareness only the slice of a larger consciousness useful for biological survival.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (consciousness is fundamental; Mishlove holds that experience cannot in principle be derived from non-conscious matter)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjectivity is basic and known directly, since consciousness is something ‘we are’. Memory, agency, personal presence, and transpersonal awareness can in some cases operate beyond ordinary sensory, spatial, and bodily limits.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualitative experience belongs to fundamental consciousness, so the hard problem is dissolved rather than solved. There is no step from insentient matter to feeling that needs explaining.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A universal mind or mentality-at-large; individual minds within it; the brain as a filtering organ; higher-dimensional mental spaces in which dream, out-of-body, near-death, and mystical experiences take place.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Mishlove draws on James’s radical empiricism, which admits direct experience and human testimony as data, alongside laboratory parapsychology and case studies of survival phenomena.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Nested levels: four-dimensional spacetime, with the body and the phenomenal world, is embedded in a higher-dimensional hyperspace, as in Saul-Paul Sirag’s formalism, and that hyperspace lies within mind-at-large.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal, Memory, Agency, Personal identity, Transpersonal and anomalous experience, Survival
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Filtration: the brain restricts access to a larger consciousness, so reduced brain activity can coincide with expanded experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness does not arise; it is present throughout and becomes localized and constrained when expressed through a brain-body system. At death the constraint lifts and experience continues.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Mind is universal. The experienced spaces of dreams, out-of-body states, and mystical states are located in a higher-dimensional space outside ordinary physical space.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness carries memory, will, and personal identity, which Mishlove, citing Wilder Penfield, holds that brain function does not fully account for. Psi phenomena show it acting beyond the body.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The brain passes on only the reduced information useful for survival. Psi and survival phenomena show information reaching or leaving a person outside the senses.
core_claims_and_evidence: Materialism cannot derive experience from lifeless matter and dualism cannot explain interaction, so idealism is the most parsimonious option.
Psychedelic states that feel more intense correlate with reduced cortical activity, and terminal lucidity appears in severely damaged brains, both as filter theory predicts.

Nine largely independent lines of evidence (including psi, near-death experiences, after-death communications, reincarnation cases, mediumship, xenoglossy, possession, and physical mediumship) together converge as a ‘bundle of arrows’ against materialism.
Following James’s white crow principle, a single well-attested case defeats the universal claim that minds cannot operate beyond the brain.
Living agent psi in its unrestricted form is unfalsifiable and so cannot serve as a scientific alternative to survival.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical (parapsychological and case-study data) combined with philosophical argument from parsimony

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Laboratory psi experiments; fMRI studies of psilocybin (Carhart-Harris and colleagues); neuroimaging of mediums; studies of terminal lucidity; case investigations of near-death experiences, reincarnation, and mediumship.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Critics point to heavy reliance on historical and anecdotal material and a brief treatment of the super-psi counter-hypothesis. The ‘leaky bucket’ objection holds that individually flawed lines of evidence cannot add up to a strong case, which Mishlove answers with P. A. Sturrock’s Bayesian analysis of convergent arguments.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The view lacks a model of how universal consciousness yields an individuated self that survives, which bears on whether it explains phenomenal consciousness or only relocates it. Mishlove concedes that reincarnation fits the children’s cases better than his own archetypal synchronistic resonance model.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The framework sits within analytic idealism and the ‘primordial tradition’ described by Huston Smith, and it is internally consistent. Its hyperspace models are speculative additions not required by the idealist core.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since the brain filters consciousness instead of producing it, Mishlove expects experience to persist after bodily death and treats survival evidence as confirming this.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Following his mentor Arthur M. Young, Mishlove holds that purpose is built into existence and that we are part of a process by which consciousness comes to know itself compassionately.
